vulnerabilities.description: The iframe rendering user-provided HTML/CSS uses sandbox="allow-scripts", which permits arbitrary JavaScript execution. While this is a feature of the HTML preview tool, it creates an XSS risk if user input is not properly escaped.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add CSP (Content Security Policy) headers to restrict script execution scope. Consider using sandbox="" (no permissions) by default and only enable specific permissions when necessary. Add visual warning that users should not paste untrusted HTML.

vulnerabilities.description: Session and memory data is stored in plaintext JSON files (.claude-flow/data/memory.json). If sensitive data is stored here, it would be vulnerable to unauthorized access.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: If sensitive data is stored, implement encryption for the JSON files. Currently, the script only stores non-sensitive configuration and session metadata, so this is low risk.

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files created for GitHub CLI operations may not be cleaned up if the process is killed (signal termination) before the finally block executes.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Implement a signal handler (SIGTERM, SIGINT) to ensure cleanup. Consider using a file descriptor-based approach or system temp directory with automatic cleanup.

vulnerabilities.description: User-provided JSON strings are parsed without size limits. A maliciously crafted JSON file could cause DoS through memory exhaustion.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Add input size validation before JSON.parse. Limit maximum JSON size to reasonable values (e.g., 1MB).

positives: ✓ No hardcoded API keys, passwords, or secrets found
✓ No SQL injection risks detected (no database queries in frontend)
✓ No direct eval() or Function() constructor usage
✓ Environment variables properly separated (NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix used correctly)
✓ No dangerous dangerouslySetInnerHTML with user input
✓ Input validation implemented for key names (regex: /^[a-z0-9_]+$/i)
✓ React components properly escaped (no direct XSS from template literals)
✓ No exposed credentials in build files or manifests
concerns: ⚠ HTML preview tool allows script execution in iframe (intentional but risky)
⚠ Plaintext JSON file storage for session data
⚠ Temporary file cleanup race condition in CLI helper
⚠ No input size validation before JSON.parse

recommendations.details: Implement max size checks before JSON.parse() in formatador-json.ts to prevent DoS attacks
Add Content Security Policy (CSP) headers and implement warning UI for HTML preview tool
Implement SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers in github-safe.js to ensure temp files are cleaned up
Add comments to memory.js warning that it's not suitable for sensitive data storage
Run 'npm audit' regularly and update dependencies, particularly qrcode package
